log.text: Tsareena used High Jump Kick → Tyranitar
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Tsareena

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar lead wins the weather war: it's slower than Politoed, so Sand Stream resolves last and overwrites Drizzle, deleting Swift Swim and rain-boosted Water damage while sand chip strips Whimsicott's Focus Sash. Sand Rush Excadrill hits 216 Speed with Life Orb to threaten Politoed/Basculegion immediately. Back: Gholdengo (Good as Gold blanks Taunt/Encore, immune to Normal Weather Ball) and Sinistcha (Heatproof vs Delphox, resists Water/Grass, Rage Powder + Strength Sap to neuter Metagross/Tsa
decisions.notebook:
Series vs rain team. Foe: Whimsicott(FocusSash,Prankster: Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast), Politoed(Drizzle,SitrusBerry,HelpingHand/IcyWind/WeatherBall/Protect), Basculegion(SwiftSwim,MysticWater,LastRespects/WaveCrash/AquaJet), Metagross(LifeOrb,ClearBody), Delphox+Delphoxite(Mega: Levitate, ~169-204 Spe), Tsareena(WideLens, QueenlyMajesty blocks our priority incl. Fake Out).
G1 lost 0-4 leading Gholdengo/Sinistcha style; G2 pivot to SAND: Tyranitar+Excadrill leads, Gholdengo+Sinistcha back.
WEATHER RULE: on-switch-in weather resolves in speed order, slower sets last. Tyranitar (81 Spe) is slower than Politoed (90-122) so sand beats Drizzle on any simultaneous entry. Politoed only re-sets rain by switching back in; they historically never switch it. Re-entering Tyranitar re-sets sand.
KEY NUMBERS: sand chips Whimsicott/Politoed/Basculegion/Delphox/Tsareena (breaks Sash; Excadrill LO Rock Slide 23-53% then finishes). Sand gives Tyranitar +50% SpD and Excadrill 216 Spe (still outrun by Tailwind Basculegion up to 260). Weatherless: Exca HH on Politoed 52-99%, on Basculegion 49-114%; Gholdengo Tbolt Basculegion 48-88%. Last Respects = 50BP x (their faints+1), 2x on Gholdengo/Sinistcha, ignores Good as Gold; delay KOing their mons while Basculegion lives. Protect chains stall rain out.

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott+Basculegion for flexible Tailwind pressure; Politoed can switch in to erase sand, activate Swift Swim, and enable Basculegion to threaten Excadrill. Tsareena provides a durable Ground-resistant attacker, strong Tyranitar pressure, and priority denial.
decisions.notebook: Opponent favors Tyranitar+Excadrill sand offense and repeated double Rock Slide. Excadrill is Life Orb Sand Rush with High Horsepower, Iron Head, Rock Slide, Protect; prioritize removing it and preserve Politoed to overwrite sand. Tyranitar has Passho Berry. Sinistcha has Rage Powder, Mental Herb, Heatproof; Taunt is unreliable immediately, while Grass attackers and spread moves bypass redirection. Gholdengo has Thunderbolt, Leftovers, and may Protect beside Excadrill when threatened, creating Encore opportunities. Floette-Eternal holds Floettite. Mr. Rime has Fake Out and Screen Cleaner. Preferred sand plan: lead Whimsicott+Basculegion, switch Whimsicott to Politoed when safe to remove sand and activate Swift Swim, with Tsareena as a Ground-resistant Tyranitar answer and priority blocker.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill (216 in sand) Rock Slide first: pops Whimsicott's Focus Sash so sandstorm chip KOs it end-of-turn (30% flinch may also deny Tailwind), and chips Basculegion 21-40%. Tyranitar Crunch (2x) adds 67-124%, so Basculegion is very likely dead too, especially with Wave Crash recoil. Worst case we trade Excadrill for Whimsicott plus a near-dead Basculegion, and Tyranitar keeps sand up with Passho covering Water hits.

Series vs rain team. Foe: Whimsicott(FocusSash,Prankster: Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, NO Protect), Politoed(Drizzle,SitrusBerry,HelpingHand/IcyWind/WeatherBall/Protect), Basculegion(SwiftSwim,MysticWater,LastRespects/WaveCrash/AquaJet/Protect), Metagross(LifeOrb,ClearBody), Delphox+Delphoxite(Mega: Levitate ~169-204 Spe), Tsareena(WideLens, QueenlyMajesty blocks our priority).
G1 lost 0-4 with Gholdengo/Sinistcha lead; G2 sand plan: TTar+Excadrill lead, Gholdengo/Sinistcha back.
WEATHER RULE: slower setter wins on simultaneous entry; TTar 81 Spe < Politoed, so sand overwrites Drizzle. Re-entering TTar re-sets sand. Politoed must switch out/in to re-rain.
KEY NUMBERS (sand): Exca 216 Spe outruns Whimsicott/Bascu/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross but NOT Tailwind Bascu or Mega Delphox. Sand chip breaks Focus Sash mons at 1 HP. Exca LO Rock Slide -> Bascu 21-40% (spread), HH -> Bascu 54-101%. TTar Crunch -> Bascu 67-124% (2x). Bascu WaveCrash OHKOs Excadrill (171-247%) guaranteed; TTar has Passho to soften one Water hit.
Last Respects = 50BP x (their faints+1), 2x vs Gholdengo/Sinistcha, ignores Good as Gold: avoid piling up faints while Basculegion lives.
Plan: prioritize removing Basculegion, then use Excadrill sand rush; Gholdengo Tbolt is good vs Politoed/Basculegion; Sinistcha Rage Powder redirects and Strength Sap neuters Metagross/Tsareena physical attackers.

decisions.rationale: Wait—Slot 2 index 0 is Gholdengo. Gholdengo is the better replacement: Good as Gold blanks Whimsicott's Prankster Taunt/Encore, Steel resists Politoed's Icy Wind and Whimsicott's Moonblast, and it threatens both foes (Make It Rain spread is 2x on Whimsicott; Thunderbolt 39-82% on Politoed). Sinistcha would be Icy Wind-weak and status-vulnerable. Correcting index below.

G1 lost 0-4. G2: TTar+Exca lead; Exca died to Bascu Wave Crash, but TTar Crunch KO'd Basculegion (Last Respects threat gone for G2).
WEATHER: slower setter wins simultaneous entry; TTar 81 Spe < Politoed so TTar sand overwrites Drizzle on re-entry. Politoed must switch out/in to re-rain.
CORRECTION: Water is NEUTRAL vs Steel (Gholdengo does not resist Water). Gholdengo resists Ice/Fairy/Grass/Psychic; weak to Fire and Ground (Delphox Heat Wave 2x, Metagross Stomping Tantrum 2x).
CALCS: Gholdengo Tbolt -> Politoed 39-82%; Politoed rain Weather Ball -> Gholdengo 34-80%. TTar Crunch -> Bascu 2x. Exca LO HH -> Bascu 54-101%.
PLAN: Good as Gold makes Gholdengo the Whimsicott answer (immune to Taunt/Encore); Make It Rain spread is 2x on Whimsicott, and sand chip breaks its Focus Sash. Sinistcha (Heatproof, Rage Powder, Strength Sap) is the Delphox/Metagross/Tsareena answer but is Ice-weak; keep Mental Herb for Taunt. Down to 3 mons vs 5: play for KOs, not chip; re-set sand with TTar when possible.

Sinistcha stays in because it's immune to HJK, resists Power Whip, and Matcha Gotcha hits Politoed 2x (32-58%, pressuring Sitrus) while healing itself; it comfortably survives Knock Off + Icy Wind (max ~79%).
decisions.notebook:
Series vs rain team. Now 3v3: mine TTar/Gholdengo/Sinistcha vs Whimsicott(FocusSash,Prankster: Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, no Protect), Politoed(Drizzle,SitrusBerry,HelpingHand/IcyWind/WeatherBall/Protect), Tsareena(WideLens,QueenlyMajesty blocks our priority; PowerWhip/HJK/KnockOff/Protect). Delphox+Metagross not brought G2. Basculegion KO'd.

Sinistcha MatchaGotcha -> Politoed 33-58%. Politoed IcyWind -> Sinistcha 17-26%. Tsareena KnockOff -> Sinistcha 36-53% (Sinistcha survives KnockOff+IcyWind). IMMUNITIES: Sinistcha and Gholdengo are both immune to HJK (Ghost) and resist Power Whip; both weak to Dark KnockOff. Gholdengo Good as Gold blanks Whimsicott Taunt/Encore. Rage Powder FAILS to redirect Grass types (Tsareena, Whimsicott). Water is neutral vs Steel.
WEATHER: slower setter wins on simultaneous entry; TTar(81) re-entering overwrites Drizzle, so pivoting TTar back in kills rain and enables sand chip to break Whimsicott's Sash.
PLAN: keep TTar hidden/protected from Tsareena until Tsareena is chipped below ~55%, then Ice Punch KO. Sinistcha tanks Tsareena/Politoed with Strength Sap/Matcha heal; Mental Herb covers Taunt. Gholdengo handles Whimsicott (Make It Rain 2x) and Politoed (Tbolt).

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand plus High Jump Kick reliably removes Tyranitar: Tsareena ignores Rage Powder as a Grass type, Wide Lens makes HJK 99% accurate, and Helping Hand offsets a possible pre-move Strength Sap. Tsareena also survives any unboosted Tyranitar attack from full.

That was offset by Tyranitar's Crunch OHKOing Basculegion the same turn, removing their rain sweeper and Swift Swim threat before it could snowball, and by Sinistcha (Grass/Ghost, Heatproof) hard-walling the remaining Politoed/Tsareena co

reflections.notebook:
Series vs rain team (I am p1) — CLOSED 2-0 (won G1 and G2). Notes retained for future encounters with this archetype/opponent.

OPPONENT COMPOSITION/BRING TENDENCY: Both games they brought Politoed + Basculegion + Whimsicott + Tsareena and benched Mega Delphox (Delphoxite) and LifeOrb Metagross — they never used their Mega Stone across the series. Lead was Whimsicott + Basculegion.

OPPONENT BEHAVIOR PATTERNS: Basculegion immediately targets my Ground/Steel physical attacker (Excadrill) with Wave Crash for a turn-1 KO. Politoed spends early turns on Helping Hand to power Tsareena rather than attacking. Tsareena uses Protect to scout when it is the lone healthy threat. Whimsicott prioritizes Tailwind over Taunt/Encore when Gholdengo (Good as Gold) is on the field. Whimsicott runs Focus Sash and no Protect, so a spread hit plus any chip removes it.

MY WORKING CALCS/FACTS: Gholdengo SpA 203 — Make It Rain spread breaks Whimsicott's Sash (98-190%), hits Tsareena 38-70%, Tbolt vs Politoed 39-82%; Make It Rain drops own SpA by 2, so don't spam. Sinistcha SpA 141 Matcha Gotcha single vs Politoed 43.7-77.6% (spread ~33-58%) and heals 50% of damage. TTar Crunch OHKOs Basculegion; Ice Punch vs Tsareena 41-75%. Tsareena HJK OHKOs TTar (117-169%) but fails/crashes vs Ghost.

MECHANICS/MATCHUP KEYS: Sinistcha (Grass/Ghost, Heatproof, Mental Herb) is the engine — immune to Normal Weather Ball, walls Politoed indefinitely, and Rage Powder bypasses Queenly Majesty (but not spread moves or Grass targets). Good as Gold blanks Taunt/Encore. As the slower weather setter, bringing TTar in late

reflections.summary: The sand lead was neutralized, but the plan traded away Basculegion—the strongest rain attacker—for Excadrill and left Politoed and Tsareena poorly positioned against Sinistcha’s sustained Matcha Gotcha pressure plus Gholdengo’s spread damage. Tyranitar’s Protect also converted the Fighting threat into High Jump Kick crash damage. The four suited the sand lead better than the Sinistcha/Gholdengo endgame; none of the brought Pokémon held a Mega Stone, so Mega Evolution was not a factor.
